description: Push-to-talk voice agent browser runtime — MediaRecorder → /api/stt → /api/llm → /api/tts round-trip with Safari/Chrome/Firefox MIME negotiation.

buildHints.whenToUse: Browser-native push-to-talk agents — mic capture, STT → LLM → TTS round-trips — where zero SDK lock-in and cross-browser compatibility matter more than server-side streaming.
firstSteps: Run `pnpm install` then `pnpm dev` — Vite serves on port 4180 (configured in vite.config.ts). The push-to-talk UI renders immediately; mic permission is requested on first button press.

Wire the three API routes documented in `api/README.md`: POST /api/stt (audio blob → { text }), POST /api/llm ({ transcript } → { reply }), POST /api/tts ({ text } → audio bytes). All logic lives in `src/main.ts`.
Run `node validate-voice.mjs` (or `pnpm validate`) to verify scaffold coherence before wiring backends.
Run `pnpm build` to emit a static bundle to `dist/` — deploy behind any CDN that serves HTTPS (required for getUserMedia outside localhost).
gotchas: getUserMedia requires HTTPS outside localhost — any plain-HTTP deployment gets NotAllowedError before the mic prompt even appears.
MediaRecorder MIME support varies by browser: Safari prefers audio/mp4, Chrome/Firefox prefer audio/webm;codecs=opus. pickMimeType() in main.ts handles this via isTypeSupported() — do not bypass it.

Safari autoplay blocks Audio.play() without a prior user gesture. The pointerdown → roundTrip() path satisfies the requirement; do not move playback into a setTimeout or async callback that escapes the gesture context.
Call track.stop() on each MediaStreamTrack when recording ends to release the mic-active indicator. main.ts does this in the 'stop' event handler — preserve that pattern if you refactor.
The /api proxy in vite.config.ts only works during `pnpm dev`. For production, route /api/* through your deployment platform (Cloudflare Workers, Vercel rewrite rules, etc.).
architectureNotes: main.ts is an intentionally single-file, no-framework runtime. All state (mediaRecorder, chunks, currentStream) is module-level — there is no component tree to wire.
The three API contracts (/api/stt, /api/llm, /api/tts) are the only integration surface — swap any backend without touching browser code.
Audio is POSTed as a raw Blob body with Content-Type from recorder.mimeType — never base64 in JSON. This keeps the STT payload at native size (~80 KB / 10 s of opus).
